---
title: "Find species missing from FFB"
format: html
---

Here we present a practical guide to the `flora_species_gap()` function of the `floraR` package. Given a genus of plants or algae, it lists the species-level names that occur in Brazil but that the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) does not register yet - a to-do list for taxonomists expanding the FFB monographs.

It combines two independent kinds of evidence that a species occurs in Brazil, from up to four sources:

- **POWO distributions** - species that [Plants of the World Online (POWO)](https://powo.science.kew.org), maintained by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, maps in Brazil;
- **Type specimens** - species whose type specimens (holotypes, isotypes, lectotypes, syntypes, paratypes, and so on) were collected in Brazil, from three collection databases: [GBIF](https://www.gbif.org), where herbaria worldwide publish their specimens; the [Reflora Virtual Herbarium](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/reflora/herbarioVirtual/); and [JABOT](https://jabot.jbrj.gov.br), the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden's herbarium system. A type collected in Brazil is direct evidence that the taxon occurs in the country.

All four sources are queried by default, and their results are merged, so as many gaps as possible are retrieved. The result is a single table, one row per name, stating which source(s) reported it. Names reported by **more sources** are listed first: they are the strongest candidates for inclusion in FFB.

## How the comparison works

1. **FFB side.** Read every name currently registered in FFB, from the locally cached FFB dataset (downloaded only when needed, as in [`flora_download()`](/articles/download_ffb_dataset.qmd)).
2. **Each source.** Retrieve the genus's species-level names - accepted names *and* synonyms - with each name's accepted name, and the evidence that it occurs in Brazil.
3. **Missing names.** Keep only the names not already in FFB. A name counts as already in FFB when either the name itself **or its accepted name** matches any FFB name, anywhere in the checklist. This matters because checklists disagree on generic placement: for example, POWO lists *Myrcia doloresensis* as a synonym of *Eugenia florida*, which FFB registers under *Eugenia*.
4. **One table.** Merge the names from all sources into one row per name.

Names are compared ignoring case, diacritics, hyphens, *y*/*i*, and the genitive *-ii*/*-i* ending, so orthographic variants are neither reported as missing nor listed twice. For example, POWO's *Luetzelburgia andrade-limae* is recognised as FFB's *L. andradelimae*, and POWO's *Myrcia aegiphylloides* is merged with GBIF's *Myrcia aegyphylloides*. Only species-level names are reported.

## Where the evidence comes from

### POWO distributions (`sources = "powo"`)

POWO's names, synonymy, and distribution maps all come from the [World Checklist of Vascular Plants (WCVP)](https://powo.science.kew.org/about-wcvp). POWO's own API blocks programmatic clients, so Kew's data is read from one of two places, chosen with `powo_source`:

| `powo_source` | What it reads | Speed |
|---|---|---|
| `"rWCVPdata"` (default) | The whole WCVP, installed locally by the [rWCVPdata](https://github.com/matildabrown/rWCVPdata) package. | Fast: every name and distribution of the genus is resolved at once, in memory. |
| `"checklistbank"` | POWO's own weekly export and WCVP, as hosted on [ChecklistBank](https://www.checklistbank.org). | Slower: one web request per candidate. Always current, and needs no extra package. |

A species has POWO evidence when its accepted name occurs in at least one of the five TDWG level-3 areas covering Brazil - Brazil North, Northeast, West-Central, Southeast, and South - the areas POWO maps. If no distribution is mapped, POWO's free-text range (e.g. `"Brazil (Bahia)"`) is checked instead; `POWO_Evidence_Source` records which was used. POWO covers vascular plants only, so it finds nothing for algae.

### GBIF type specimens (`sources = "gbif"`)

The genus is searched among plants and algae only - the GBIF kingdoms Plantae (land plants, red and green algae), Chromista (brown algae, diatoms), and Protozoa (euglenids) - so a genus name shared with an animal, such as *Gracilaria* (both a red alga and a moth), resolves to the alga. A single search lists every name in the genus with type specimens collected in Brazil; for the FFB-missing names only, the specimens themselves are then retrieved and summarised.

### REFLORA and JABOT type specimens (`sources = "reflora"`, `"jabot"`)

The specimens of the genus are read with the [refloraR](https://github.com/DBOSlab/refloraR) and [jabotR](https://github.com/DBOSlab/jabotR) packages, from the Darwin Core archives of the herbaria in REFLORA and JABOT. The names of the specimens collected in Brazil that are types - with any type status - are compared with FFB, and each missing name comes with a summary of its types, and, for REFLORA, links to the specimens' pages. As in GBIF, a specimen is filed under its current identification.

In all three specimen sources, type statuses are standardised with `std_types()` from [barRoso](https://github.com/DBOSlab/barRoso) - so `"HOLOTYPUS"`, `"Holotype"`, and `"holótipo"` all become `"holotype"` - and places with its `std_place()`.

### Keeping the downloaded archives (`keep_downloads`)

The REFLORA and JABOT archives are big: the first analysis downloads several gigabytes to two folders in your working directory, `reflora_download/` and `jabot_download/`, which takes a while. By default (`keep_downloads = TRUE`) these folders are **kept**, so any new analysis - for the same genus or another one - reuses them instead of downloading everything again. Reading them still takes a few minutes per call, so to check several genera, give them all in one call (see [Several genera in one call](#several-genera-in-one-call)): the archives are then read only once.

If you only need one analysis, or want to keep the working directory clean and light, set `keep_downloads = FALSE`: the folders are deleted once the analysis is finished.

```r
# Delete the REFLORA and JABOT archives after this analysis
gap <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia", keep_downloads = FALSE)
```

## Installing rWCVPdata, refloraR, and jabotR

`rWCVPdata` is not on CRAN. Install it once with:

```r
install.packages("rWCVPdata",
                 repos = c("https://matildabrown.github.io/drat",
                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

The WCVP version in use is shown in each HTML report; `rWCVPdata::wcvp_check_version()` tells you whether a newer release is available. If you prefer not to install it, use `powo_source = "checklistbank"`, or leave `"powo"` out of `sources`.

`refloraR` and `jabotR` are installed from GitHub; without them, REFLORA or JABOT is skipped with a message:

```r
remotes::install_github(c("DBOSlab/refloraR", "DBOSlab/jabotR"))
```

## Find species missing from FFB

```r
library(floraR)

gap <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia")
```

This returns one row per missing name, and also saves an `.xlsx` spreadsheet and a self-contained HTML report (KPI counts plus a filterable table you can copy or download) in the `flora_species_gap/` folder. With POWO and GBIF alone (`sources = c("powo", "gbif")`), 28 names of *Myrcia* are missing from FFB: 6 reported by both - such as *Myrcia microcalyx*, mapped by POWO in Brazil North and known from a holotype and isotypes collected there - 4 by POWO only, and 18 by GBIF only. REFLORA and JABOT add the types kept in Brazilian herbaria.

Key columns of the result:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Taxon_name`, `Authors`, `Accepted_name` | The name, its authors, and its accepted name. |
| `Found_in` | The sources that reported the name, e.g. `"POWO; GBIF; REFLORA"`, `"GBIF; JABOT"`, or `"POWO"`. |
| `Brazil_evidence` | Whether POWO places the species in Brazil or it has Brazilian types. |
| `POWO_Brazil_Areas`, `POWO_Evidence_Source` | The Brazilian regions POWO maps for the species, and whether from the WCVP distribution or POWO's range text. |
| `POWO_Published_in`, `POWO_URL`, `IPNI_URL` | Protologue citation, and links to the name's POWO and IPNI pages. |
| `GBIF_N_type_specimens`, `GBIF_Type_statuses` | Number of type specimens collected in Brazil, and their categories. |
| `GBIF_Type_specimens` | Up to ten specimens, as herbarium, catalogue number, and type status. |
| `GBIF_Specimen_names` | The names the types are filed under in GBIF - usually the typified name. |
| `GBIF_Collectors`, `GBIF_Years`, `GBIF_States` | Who collected the types, when, and in which Brazilian states. |
| `GBIF_URL` | Link to the name's GBIF page. |
| `REFLORA_*`, `JABOT_*` | For each herbarium source: `N_type_specimens`, `Type_statuses`, `Type_specimens`, `Collectors`, `Years`, `States`, and `Links` (REFLORA only). |

Source-specific columns are `NA` for names that source did not report.

## Read the typification

`GBIF_Specimen_names` shows which name each type actually belongs to, which often differs from `Taxon_name`. For example, in *Myrcia* the row for *Myrcia aegiphylloides* (reported by both sources) rests on a holotype collected in Rio de Janeiro that GBIF files under *Aulomyrcia anomala* O.Berg - pointing straight to the basionym and its original material.

## Several genera in one call

`taxon` also takes a vector of genera. Reading the REFLORA and JABOT archives is the slow step, and it is done only **once** for all of them (as is reading FFB and WCVP), so one call with ten genera is much faster than ten separate calls:

```r
gap_many <- flora_species_gap(taxon = c("Myrcia", "Eugenia", "Calyptranthes"))
```

Each genus is analysed separately, and gets its own spreadsheet and HTML report in `dir`, named after it - `flora_species_gap_Myrcia.xlsx`, `flora_species_gap_Eugenia.html`, and so on. The returned table stacks the candidates of all genera. A genus that fails (e.g. a misspelling) is reported and skipped, without stopping the others.

## Genera with nothing missing

A genus whose species with evidence are all already in FFB needs no FFB update, so it gets **no** spreadsheet or detailed report. Instead, all such genera of a call are listed together in one simple page, `__no_missing_species_report.html` in `dir` (the leading underscores keep it at the top of the folder). For each genus it shows its number of species in FFB, the number of names with evidence in each source, and a conclusion:

| Conclusion | Meaning |
|---|---|
| All names already in FFB - no update needed | The sources reported names, and FFB already has all of them. |
| No names found - check the genus | The sources returned nothing - often a misspelt genus. |

So, after checking a list of genera, the folder holds one spreadsheet and one report per genus that needs an FFB update, and this single page for the rest.

## Choose the sources

```r
# A quick check, without the REFLORA and JABOT archives
gap_quick <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia", sources = c("powo", "gbif"))

# Brazilian herbaria only
gap_herbaria <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia", sources = c("reflora", "jabot"))

# POWO only, read live from ChecklistBank
gap_powo <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia", sources = "powo",
                              powo_source = "checklistbank")

# GBIF only - e.g. for algae, which POWO does not cover
gap_algae <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Gracilaria", sources = "gbif")

# Stricter type evidence: holotypes and isotypes only
gap_strict <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia", type_status = c("Holotype", "Isotype"))

# Also review POWO names missing from FFB that POWO places outside Brazil
gap_all <- flora_species_gap(taxon = "Myrcia", require_brazil_evidence = FALSE)
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Applies to | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `taxon` | | One or more genus names of plants or algae; see [Several genera in one call](#several-genera-in-one-call). |
| `sources` | | Any of `"powo"`, `"gbif"`, `"reflora"`, and `"jabot"`. Default: all four. |
| `keep_downloads` | REFLORA, JABOT | If `TRUE` (default), keep the downloaded `reflora_download/` and `jabot_download/` folders for later analyses; if `FALSE`, delete them afterwards. |
| `powo_source` | POWO | `"rWCVPdata"` (default) or `"checklistbank"`. |
| `require_brazil_evidence` | POWO | If `TRUE` (default), keep only POWO names placed in Brazil. |
| `fetch_details` | POWO | With `powo_source = "checklistbank"`, fetch each candidate's protologue citation. Default `TRUE`. |
| `max_number` | POWO | With `powo_source = "checklistbank"`, maximum number of names retrieved. Default `5000`. |
| `type_status` | GBIF | Type categories counted as evidence (e.g. `c("Holotype", "Isotype")`). `NULL` (default) uses all. |
| `version` | | FFB dataset version to compare against. Default `"latest"`. |
| `save`, `dir` | | Save each genus's result as an `.xlsx` spreadsheet, named `flora_species_gap_<genus>.xlsx`, and where; genera with nothing missing get none (see [Genera with nothing missing](#genera-with-nothing-missing)). |
| `html_report`, `open_report` | | Write the HTML report, and (with `open_report = TRUE`) open it in the browser. |
| `verbose` | | Print progress messages. Default `TRUE`. |

## Additional Tips

- Start with the names reported by more sources (e.g. `Found_in == "POWO; GBIF; REFLORA"`): independent lines of evidence point to the same gap.
- A synonym reported as missing usually means FFB lacks its accepted name too; check `Accepted_name` before adding a name.
- GBIF names with `GBIF_Taxonomic_status` `"DOUBTFUL"` are often old names of uncertain application (e.g. many 19th-century names): filter them out for a shorter list, or review them if you are revising the group.
- GBIF, REFLORA, and JABOT only know the types that herbaria have digitised and published; a name absent from the result may still have Brazilian types in a collection not yet in them.
- The HTML report requires the `rmarkdown`, `DT`, and `htmltools` packages. Without them, the report is skipped with a message and the spreadsheet is still saved.
